quote: And then Kellina, please please tell me Kellina. It's not Michelina. Okay?
stewart_read: Customer corrects her name assertively; rep's recovery at 00:29 ('Please. Say that one more time.') and repeating it back at 00:35 is an adequate, low-cost repair — customer does not raise it again and stays cooperative for the rest of the call.
coaching_implication: No action needed — this is a clean example of a small friction point being closed quickly. Worth noting as a positive micro-recovery if the manager is looking for what this rep does well.

quote: Because my my electricity bill is high, and, anyway, I want anything good for the environment.
stewart_read: Customer names bill pain directly as her top reason for interest — the exact emotional anchor the schema flags as highest-value. Rep's response folds it into a generic acknowledgment about clean energy rather than flagging it as something to come back to.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly reflect the bill-pain reason back later when discussing usage/design ('since your bill's been running high, this design will show you exactly where that lands') instead of only validating it once and moving on.

quote: I am seeing some pretty tall trees around your home there. Are all those trees still there?
stewart_read: Customer reveals the trees were recently cut and the roof is new and in full sun — both improve solar viability and are exactly the kind of enthusiasm signal the schema flags as easy to walk past.
coaching_implication: Rep did ask and got the useful answer (trees removed, roof new, full sun) — good verify execution. Coach to explicitly flag this to the closer in the handoff as a positive site-condition signal, since it materially improves the lead's viability.

quote: Only requirement is that you have a credit score above 6 170.
stewart_read: Rep states the credit threshold as '6 170' (likely a mangled '670' per the schema's stated 670 threshold, though transcription is ambiguous). This is a verbal stumble rather than a stated wrong number like the 650 drift seen in other calls, but it lands unclear to the customer.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a transcription artifact of the rep clearly saying '670' and Deepgram mis-rendering it; not strong enough to call a schema drift on its own.
coaching_implication: Flag for the manager to listen to the audio directly at 02:36 — if the rep is genuinely stumbling on the credit number, it's worth a quick clarity coaching note since qualifier numbers need to land unambiguously.

quote: I would have to get on the site and look. I don't have anything.
stewart_read: Customer clearly signals she doesn't have bill data on hand and would need to search online, but the rep continues probing for a paper bill for another minute-plus (04:04, 05:09) before pivoting to the utility-call/online-lookup path at 06:02. This exceeds the schema's 2-minute pivot budget for friction resolution.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have been reactively following the customer's own lead as she rummaged through her files rather than independently prolonging it — she volunteers 'wait, I have my file here' at 04:18, pulling the rep back into the paper search.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to proactively redirect once the customer signals uncertainty ('I don't know, I'd have to look') rather than continuing to co-search live — offer the deferred path (call utility / check online / text bill later) within the 2-minute window even if the customer is still digging through papers.

quote: what we'll do is we'll set up, a meeting. So it'll actually just be, like, a phone call meeting, and then we'll have a specialist give you a call.
stewart_read: Rep gestures at setting up a meeting but never states a day or time, never blocks an hour, never asks the 'is that fair?' handshake, and never confirms the wife (co-title-holder) will be present. The call ends on an email-exchange promise instead of a locked appointment.
coaching_implication: This is the single biggest structural gap on the call — no button-up occurred at all. Coach the rep to always land on a specific date/time before ending the call, even if bill collection is still pending; the appointment can be set contingent on bill arrival rather than left completely open.

stewart_read: Customer confirms her wife is a co-owner on the title. Rep acknowledges and logs it ('Okay. No problem. We'll go ahead and put that down here') but never circles back to confirm the wife will be included on the eventual specialist call.
alternative_hypothesis: Since no appointment time was ever set, there was no concrete moment left in this call to schedule the wife's presence — the omission may simply be a downstream consequence of the unanchored exit rather than a standalone spouse-protocol failure.
coaching_implication: Once the rep begins locking an actual appointment time (which didn't happen here), they must explicitly ask which times work for both the customer and her wife. Flag this as a to-do for whoever follows up on this lead.
